utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning, Your Honour. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The Chamber was informed that the Prosecution wished to raise a matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Your Honours, yesterday you noted that Dr. Turkusic has been called as a fact witness but that his factual knowledge and observations are intertwined with his technical background and experience. And I've asked to address you this morning before the witness is brought in to request that if the witness is going to be asked to opine about incidents that he has no personal knowledge of, that he be provided the relevant information to make his opinion useful, either the investigation file or the conclusions of his fellow KDZ colleagues. Yesterday, at transcript page 15762, the Defence showed the witness a photo of an impact in the side of a wall, represented to the witness that this impact was caused by a mortar, and asked the witness's opinion as to the direction of fire. This photo was from scheduled incident G13 and, as the Defence knows, the documents accompanying that photo indicate that the impact was caused by a rotating artillery projectile and not a mortar. With nothing more than this photograph and this false premise, the witness speculated for several pages about the direction of fire that might be if a mortar had left that impact. We submit that littering the transcript with this kind of speculation has no probative value. If it is the Defence case that the underlying investigation file is incorrect and that the impact was caused by a mortar, the Defence should put that case to the witness pursuant to Rule 90(H) and provide the witness with enough information to make an informed opinion. And so I would just like to ask -- request an instruction from the Chamber that for the remainder of this witness's cross-examination, if the Defence wishes to elicit opinions that the witness be provided with sufficient information on which to form them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Harbour. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would be very happy to exclude any opinions, and that's what we asked from this witness, and that's what we asked in our motions. I don't see any necessity for the Prosecution to defend this witness. We have the right to ask him. He should have noticed that it's not a mortar shell. According to the traces and according to the expert witnesses we employed, it is mortar shell. There was no any rotating artillery projectile. And I can ask him now when he enters. I can go back to that issue and ask him what he thinks: Was it mortar or was it artillery projectile. We can clarify with him very easily and I will do it immediately upon his arrival.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, what you said is not an answer to the request of Ms. Harbour. Ms. Harbour asks that if you are eliciting opinion evidence from the witness, then to provide him with all relevant factual information. That's what she asks. And I would like to hear your response to that request.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I told you my response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just to add to what Judge Orie has said, Mr. Lukic, it is improper cross-examination to mislead a witness. Just hold on. Let me finish. If it is your case that it is a mortar -- if occasioned by a mortar, you put it to him that that is your case and ask him whether he agrees with you. You don't tell him that it is caused by a mortar and then --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will do it that way, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's fine. Thank you. And that's part of the Prosecution's request, that if facts that are truthful to him and let him opine on them, okay? But don't give him misleading facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: With respect to this particular incident if it's helpful in providing the witnesses the under-- with the underlying information, the KDZ report for this incident is at Exhibit P495, pages 10 and 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic as always is invited to remain seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The request of Ms. Harbour is granted. So, therefore, Mr. Lukic, you know what you'll have to put to the witness. Any other preliminary matter? If not, let me just -- we'll ask the witness to be escorted into the courtroom in a minute, not immediately. I'll tell you when we are there because I first would like to deal with another matter, a matter which is -- is also some urgency because the Chamber understands that the Defence has filed a request to enlarge time for filing a 94 bis response to the report of Ms. Tabeau. Now, I had already something I would like to communicate with the parties. Mr. Lukic, I will read a prepared statement. If your request from this morning would interfere with that, we will then further consider that, but I leave it so this is without having knowledge of the content of your request which was filed this morning. On the 21st of August, the Defence has filed a motion seeking to enlarge the time for filing its notice of objection in relation to Witness Ewa Tabeau on the basis that it has not yet received B/C/S translations of all of the underlying documents. On the 23rd of August, the Prosecution filed its response, accepting that it only submitted documents to the CLSS for translation on the 21st of August which was an error on the part of the Prosecution. However, it disputes the actual number of documents requiring translation. On the 25th of August, by informal communication, the Prosecution advised the Chamber that while some of the relevant documentation will be translated by the end of August, some of the documents will not be translated until the 9th of September, that is the first day of the same week in which the witness is due to testify. On the 26th of August, by a formal addendum to its response, the Prosecution informed the Chamber that Witness Tabeau is potentially available to testify in the month of November. The Chamber instructs the Prosecution to advise it in a formal filing when it has provided the Defence with all of the necessary translations in B/C/S and further decides that the Defence will have 30 days from the date it has received the translations to file its notice of objection. The Prosecution is instructed to schedule the witness's testimony accordingly, which, from their filing of the 26th of August, would most likely mean in the month of November. Mr. Lukic, if your filing of today interferes with what the Chamber had decided already, we would like to know so that we can pay further attention to it. If it covers the matter because I do understand it was a request to enlarge the time for filing a 94 bis response, then --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The ruling covers our --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The ruling covers it. Then we consider -- I hereby declare then your -- this morning's request moot. Then could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Turkusic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration that you've given at the beginning of your testimony, that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Turkusic.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have been instructed this morning to clarify one issue with you tackled yesterday, and for that we need P497. We need page 5 in the document in the B/C/S and page 1 in the English. You would remember that my main question regarding this issue whether the tail of the shell or the mine was lower or above the top. However, the Prosecution is insisting that I clarify with you whether you can offer an opinion as to whether this is a mortar shell or an artillery shell.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I'd like to object to this because again it calls for speculation. The request was that the relevant information on which to base an opinion be provided to the witness before eliciting an opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: They have right to redirect. If they are not satisfied they can clarify it themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The ruling was that the request was granted, so therefore you should put all the relevant information to the witness who has no knowledge of this incident and then you can ask him questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that an open question is a most proper one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know if that report is correct either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the fact that there is a report and what the report says is something that should be brought to the attention of the witness. The ruling is clear. Whether you consider another type of questioning more appropriate is not relevant at this moment after the ruling. Please proceed and put to the witness -- and --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't have that document with me. I cannot put the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you can deal with the matter after the break and you can find the relevant information. Most preferable would be if you and Ms. Harbour would sit together and that Ms. Harbour tells you what, in her opinion, should be put to the witness in relation to this incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And Ms. Harbour has provided you with a document number. It's P495.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In that case, we are going to leave this subject aside for the moment. Just a moment, please. Yesterday, we spoke hypothetically a lot but I'm going to put a very specific question now to you. You spoke about different surfaces, the firmness, the hardness. This shell that landed at Markale on the 28th of August, 1995, under the angle not less than 60 degrees, not less than 67 degrees, in this specific instance, would it have been embedded into the asphalt had the charge, the propelling charge, been number 4 or number 5 or number 6?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, given the type of fuse, which is impact fuse, which is activated immediately, it wouldn't have embedded into the surface in any of the cases you listed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. In the professional literature that you used, did you use the Berezanski formulae that precisely speak about the penetration and piercing of different surfaces?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you have your statement in front of you?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We need above paragraph 10, which reads determining direction and angle of fire. I have a general question: When you conducted investigations, did you determine the distance between the explosion from the potential military targets?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the location where the shell landed, according to my knowledge, there was not a single potential military target or a brigade HQ or any military fortification. That was the inner city, urban part of the centre of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You are talking about Markale 2 now; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the same applies to number 1, because the distance between these two locations is about 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question was general. Did you check, in general terms, whether a shell fell in the vicinity of any military facility?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a special police unit who had very specific tasks, did not have either jurisdiction or the need to know the disposition of potential military targets or HQs. Therefore, that was not the topic of our consideration. On the other hand, we know for sure, as do others, that this was the very centre of the city and the most frequented location in terms of the concentration of population.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You told us that this was not part of your task. I understood it to be that you limited yourself to the technical aspects. You didn't consider the vicinity of military targets. Once you've answered that question, there is no need to elaborate on other matters which you may consider relevant but which, as far as we understand, was not a specific part of your task. So would you refrain from that and limit your answer to what has been asked. Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you agree with me that there were over 2.000 legitimate military targets in Sarajevo? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Especially not according to the criteria that you believe them to be military targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: According to you, would the HQ of the Main Staff of the ABH be a military target?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that. Let me ask you: How far is the Svjetlost building from Markale and the point of impact of the shell? Which building is right across it?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are talking about the Svjetlost publishing house?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's close by.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Less than 50 metres; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly. But no shell can harm it. Any shell cannot damage it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll get back to this. Let me just briefly go over paragraph 13 of your statement with you where you speak about the accuracy of mortars as a type of weapon. You say that you're convinced that mortar fire is one of the most precise activities pursued by means of use of artillery weapons?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you say that among those who studied mortars and who were in the army and fired shells, they usually say that a mortar shell can hit a chimney on a house should you wish to do so?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me just show you the rules of mortar. I have found 82 millimetres, and that is 1D1205. The first page is rather dark and therefore probably illegible. Since we do not have a translation yet, it's still in progress, we are going only to use the table which says, "Rule, 82 millimetre mortar"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need page 10 of this document. One before this one. We need the top table on the right-hand-side page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This table deals with the coverage of targets --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, there is no English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is no English translation but I will read everything that is said in this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My problem is -- I'll try to find it. What you want to read doesn't necessarily always provide the context at which, of course, the Chamber will look as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The column of the left says that the degree of neutralisation of the target, and it goes between 15 and 25 per cent and 50 per cent in all three columns. On the right-hand side we see the degree of the shield provided for the target and we have three categories there: Outside the shield, incomplete shield, and complete shield. The number of average targets outside the shield and the number of mines or shells; we have the same information for incomplete shield, the number of targets and the number of shells; and complete shield, we also have the number of average targets and the number of shells. Outside the shield is a situation when someone is, for example, standing in the middle of a football pitch?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And throughout the entire city of Sarajevo as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Don't you think that Markale was the situation of complete shield because that location was not visible from any point?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday I said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, for the Chamber to understand this testimony, we need first an explanation of what exactly the terms are standing for. "Neutralisation," what does that mean? "Shield," what does that mean? And then we can try to understand the tables.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but since we don't have a translation, I was just intending to ask the witness whether he would agree with me and whether they had this information available that say that for neutralising a target --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if you would introduce the terminology you're using yourself, if you say I ask you about neutralisation, I use the word neutralisation to mean the following, then you define what you understand by neutralisation, and then you can ask questions. But then at least the Chamber knows what the language you are using stands for. Ms. Harbour you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Yes. In addition to the Chamber's concerns, I note from the table of contents that this is found in a section -- please excuse my pronunciation, but entitled "grupno gadzanje." And just a very quick translation, that appears to mean "group ranges," so perhaps if the Defence could also establish the context in which this section appears before putting the questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's of course the reason why -- Mr. Mladic, Mr. Mladic, would you remain seated and switch off the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to read this out so that we would know what is being discussed. Paragraph 426, on the left-hand side of this page, could we please see that as well. This is what is written: "Neutralisation fire makes it impossible to move to open fire and to conduct other activities against enemy personnel and firing assets for a certain amount of time while simultaneously inflicting losses upon them." Then 427: "The method of group targeting when neutralising enemy personnel and firing assets depends on: The degree of neutralisation, the certain amount of time that fire took for neutralisation, the type, importance, degree of cover and the position of the target, the degree of persistence of the target, and the requirements and needs of one's own infantry and the time available."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, what you just read underlines my concern. Neutralisation is not about accuracy but neutralisation is apparently about the effect of a shell fired under the circumstances given. These are two distinct matters. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: They are connected as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'll have to establish that, to what extent accuracy of the firing and the effect, either in the open field, either in an urban environment, troops being targeted, a specific matter being targeted, what then exactly the connection is and what the relation is. Of course, if you want to do that, there is no objection to that, but that is what is required.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 428.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Mr. Lukic will have to read considerably slower. This is highly complex subject matter that does not readily lend itself to simultaneous interpretation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, would you please --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I heard it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You heard it. That's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "When one wishes to make it impossible for the enemy to observe and to fire for a certain amount of time, then a lower degree of neutralisation is applied, from 15 to 25 per cent. When greater losses are supposed to be inflicted upon the enemy, in addition to preventing observation and firing, then a higher degree of neutralisation is applied, from 26 to 35 per cent. If the enemy exhibits a high degree of combat persistence, then the highest degree of neutralisation is applied, from 40 to 50 per cent." Now, the answer is in paragraph 429: "The use of shells per average target after correction, given a certain degree of neutralisation, as well as the number of average targets that a mortar platoon may neutralise by using a combat kit of ammunition is displayed in table 10." I tried to move on to this table 10 immediately and to ask the witness whether he would agree that the least amount spent would be 24 shells, if we want to stop the enemy for a certain period of time. So that is the category between 15 and 25 per cent from the first sentence of paragraph 428, and then all the way up to 216 shells if we wish to have neutralisation of 40 to 50 per cent of the target.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question has to do with your statement: Did you find this in a military textbook or a rule that a target can be destroyed with one shell?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the official rules for using any artillery piece, it does not say that one shell can destroy a certain number if we are talking about destroying the enemy. However, you put a few questions to me and I think that I have the right to answer them. A counter-question now: Would you agree, if you were driving a Mercedes that you should use instructions for an Renault car?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Now both speakers are speaking, we don't understand either one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You should not speak at the same time within limits because I think it was a rhetoric question rather than a real question for you to answer, Mr. Lukic. The witness may use that but if you would have said that if you use the non-applicable manuals, because that was what you hinted at, if I understood you well, then that doesn't work. Is that what you meant to say by referring to the Mercedes and the Renault?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is what I meant. Mr. Lukic is showing us tables and instructions for an 82-millimetre mortar whereas the shell that fell in Markale is 120-millimetres. These are two types of artillery pieces and they have different tables. As for the previous paragraphs that he quoted, it is clear that a legitimate military target, or, rather, enemy personnel, it was the population that was considered to be that, that was the character of the war in Sarajevo. Namely, they considered the entire population to be enemy personnel. So the Defence lawyer leads us to this conclusion as he quoted these previous paragraphs because it strictly says enemy personnel. So then that turned out to be the population. So that would be the character of the war in Sarajevo. As for persistence that is referred to here in one of these paragraphs, when the enemy displays persistence, this is the persistence of the population of Sarajevo to survive and to defend themselves. That's persistence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you answer my question now?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The previous question that you put? Whether one can target a --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Both speakers are speaking at the same time again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This previous has nothing to do with my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you perhaps phrase again precisely, concisely, clearly, the question you wish the witness to answer at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you come across rules for a 120-millimetre mortar, an 82-millimetre mortar and a 60-millimetre mortar that prescribe that a target can be destroyed by using a single shell?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question is what a target is and what destruction is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Have you come across any rules? Tell me. In such and such a rule it says that a single shell can destroy a target. I will accept that.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in a single manual does it say a large concentration of people in a marketplace is a target. So I cannot answer that. However, you are trying to stop me from answering the first question that was put.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That was my first question.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first question was: How can a mortar fire at a target that is covered or shielded and that cannot be seen? Can I answer? That's what you asked me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Go ahead. No, I actually asked you whether you found rules speaking of shielded targets, and in your view how many shells are required for destroying a shielded target?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In all armies of the world it's obvious that howitzers are firing at targets they cannot see.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We could not hear Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you continue this way, I have to serve as a traffic agent; that is, you may speak now, you may speak now. I give you a last opportunity to do it for yourselves. Mr. Lukic, I always asked -- I asked to be -- to explain to us what the meaning of the language is. "Shielded target," could you, when you use that expression, could you tell us exactly what you mean by it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A protected target is a target that cannot be seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's, yes, shielding could -- but you say it's -- cannot be seen. Now, let's try to understand your question and let's see whether we can get an answer to that. Mr. Lukic is interested to know whether you found anywhere a manual or -- which would express that firing one single mortar shell would be sufficient to hit a defined target. I'm not yet at this moment saying what target. Let's make the target, Mr. Lukic, a building. Is that -- because we know that military targets can also be troops where the size, of course, is maybe quite different. Let's make it a building of 10 by 10 metres. Is that -- okay. Did you find anywhere that one mortar shell would be sufficient to hit a target, and we take for a target a building of 10 by 10 metres. Did you find anything of the kind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is impossible to find something like that written somewhere but that is not to say that it is altogether impossible. It is absolutely possible because complete instructions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take it one by one. So that is found nowhere. And what you say is you wouldn't -- that would be not something you would expect to be described. Could I ask you, then, a question: What, under normal circumstances, how many shells you would need to hit such a building, that means firing one shell, adjust after having observed whether or not it hit the target, what would be, on average, the number of shells you would need at medium range to hit such a target?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In an unknown area, it follows the procedure that you described, Your Honour, roughly. However, in an area that has been well known for four or five years, where all had been mapped up to a centimetre, where the location of each garage, each building, each street is very well known, the co-ordinates are there, including one of the most important things, and that is to say the difference in altitude from the location where the mortar is and where the target is. The vertical difference in altitude is very important for targeting. It is possible to use a single shell and to hit a target without any problem whatsoever. However, the first question that I haven't managed to answer yet is the key question, the one that was put by Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will take it one by one. You say it depends on the knowledge, accurate knowledge, of the area where the target is found, whether you will be successful with your first shell fired. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since according to estimates of international military observers over a million shells fell on Sarajevo, there was a vast degree of experience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, we are still in the hypothetical. You would agree, at least I understand your testimony to be, that it is a decisive -- it's a very important factor with what precision you have the co-ordinates of targets, et cetera. Is that for the first --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The most important of all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Are there other factors which would make, or at least create a risk that you would not hit the target with your first shell, such as, and the Chamber has heard about atmospheric circumstances, for example, temperature. Would that -- would that -- could that cause to miss the target because they are unknown and not standardised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is another factor that was certainly well known in this factor and that is the difference in altitude above sea level.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Instead of saying that there are other factors, I asked you whether this would be one factor, atmospheric circumstances. Is it a factor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, wind, for instance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Wind, for instance. Now, you said altitude above sea level. Would you consider that to be --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The difference in altitude between the firing position and the location of descent because a mortar can fire at a higher altitude and a lower altitude, and this is such a case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the parabola of flight can have one side that is shorter or longer. On a horizontal plane, both sides of the parabola, if we look at the trajectory of the shell, are the same. If a shell falls at a location that is at an altitude above sea level that is lower than that of where it was fired, then it is longer and then if the target is higher, then it is shorter, and according to the tables, that is taken into account as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That, I think you are now returning to known and fixed circumstances. Altitude doesn't change. The altitude of the target remains the same. Could we now go back to Mr. Lukic's question. Mr. Lukic, you wanted to know, and that's where it all started, the accuracy of the firing of mortars. The witness has explained to us that there are known circumstances, for example, co-ordinates sometimes known of a target, a target could be a lot of things, buildings, could be troops, could be a vehicle, could be -- and there are factors which are varying, such as atmospheric circumstances. Could be temperature, could be wind. So that's where we are at this moment. Please proceed and try to keep matters clear and straight. And I add to this that the tables that you were using were not about accuracy. If a shell lands somewhere, it may have a certain effect within a certain distance, and if you want to neutralise vehicles, persons, et cetera, you may need, depending on the target, more or less shells to do that, which is not the same as where the first shell should necessarily land. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, subtitle C, paragraph 17 of your statement, we can have it maybe on our screens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's P2009.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm not going to read it. Here you speak about modified air-bombs and you say that they are relatively precise if they are dropped from an aircraft. I would like to ask you this: According to you, is an air-bomb more precise if it is dropped from an aircraft than the one that was launched by the use of a rocket engines on the ground?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to remind you that you didn't allow me to give you an answer to your first question with regard to the accuracy from the previous exchange of questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please just answer what I'm asking you now. And as for that, we shall see with the Prosecution if they want to pursue this matter or maybe I'll get back to it.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, as for your question that you put to me just now, I'm claiming the following: During one flight, an aircraft can drop an air-bomb and destroy a bridge. In another instance, my submission is that three modified air-bombs that we are talking about here, fired in sequence, a couple of minutes apart, will not hit the same place. The difference between the places where they land would be between 50 and 200 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your view, whenever an aircraft drops a bomb, it will always fall at the same place?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the pilot is an experienced one, then it will.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So we had no use to develop rocket systems, we could have used -- air-bombs are always to target the same targets?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You couldn't have done that because there was a no-fly zone imposed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's time for the break, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's time for the break. Could I urge you to always again be very precise in your language. We are talking about air-bombs dropped from planes. We are talking about air-bombs, modified air-bombs, fired by -- from the ground. Could we always be very precise because to say a pilot who is experienced could fire from the same place, one of the problems is that aeroplanes usually don't stay in the same place. They move. So, therefore, the whole comparison between the two, I did understand your second part of your question to be that if you use a modified air-bomb fired from the ground, that if you do not change the -- any direction or angle or whatever, you just fire three times from that same position, with the same -- same circumstances, that there would be a variation in where those air-bombs would land. Is that what you intended to tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I'm trying to say, and there will definitely be deviations in these three situations where we have the firing under the same circumstances and conditions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I urge you all to be precise and focused. We take a break, but we'll first have the witness be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break and we resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you may proceed, and Mr. Mladic is invited to lower the volume of his voice. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm going to go back to a question, and then we'll move to the specific incidents starting from Simon Bolivar school. Judge Orie was right when he observed that my question was not precise enough when I asked you if it is possible for an aircraft to hit the same place with several projectiles because the plane is on the move.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the answer? It was overlapping.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wouldn't agree with you in terms of precision of firing from an aircraft. An aircraft is on the move and it -- exercising hitting the same target.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I appreciate that you don't agree but I needed to ask you this question. So in your view in a number of flights an aircraft can drop an air-bomb or a bomb on one and the same location?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you want to speak about accuracy and precision, which are similar but different notions, we can discuss that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you used it as an introduction to your question. Perhaps you would pursue the question you would like to ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So, according to you, is an aircraft dropping bombs in several flights engaging the same target, is it more precise than air-bombs launched from a launching pad and propelled by rockets?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I said that we are now going to move to specific incidents. Let's first talk about the Simon Bolivar school. These are paragraphs 24 through 27 of your statement. You took part in the investigation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have 1D1200 on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will first kindly ask you to mark certain things on this photo. Can you please mark with number 1, the elementary school Simon Bolivar, and with number 2, the gym?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, this is the school looking after it's being rebuilt because it was completely destroyed at the very beginning of the war. This sign to the left, the green one, with the inscription Tus is the supermarket that has built several shops in Sarajevo in the last few years. So this is how this school looks today. From the angle that the photo was taken I'm trying to establish where -- no, I cannot see the gym from this angle unless this is the one in the foreground, the biggest part of the facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's right.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: However, the incident happened opposite the gym, inside the school. If you would like me to mark it, then this would be approximately here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were you now marking the gym or were you marking the location where the school was?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you marking the point of impact?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is the entire school where this bigger white facility is a gym, which is an integral part of the school, the rest of the building is where the classrooms are so what I marked is the side of the gym that is not visible from this point, so there was an open area there where the incident that we are discussing took place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, Mr. Lukic, so that we can follow your examination, can we just get the witness to do what you asked him to do. Can you put the 1 on the school and can he put the 2 on the gym, if he can.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please, you heard His Honour Judge Moloto, can you please mark the school with number 1 and the gym with number 2?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: However, number 1 encompasses both the left and right side, but the gym itself is marked with the number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In that case, did the explosive device hit the gym or this open area, or was it on the wall of the gym?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are talking about this incident, there are very detailed photographs and sketches from previous analyses. Therefore, this picture is almost rendered unusable for discussing this incident from this very point of view.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We chose this photograph in order to ask you if it is possible for you to determine the approximate direction towards the barracks in Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Witness, the question was very simple. Did the explosive device hit the gym or this open area? Or was it on the wall of the gym? That has nothing to do with the photograph in front of you. Could you answer that simple question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I could. And if necessary, I can use this same picture and draw the trajectory of the shell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Just answer the question Mr. Lukic has put to you, which I repeated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the shell hit the wall of the gym at the place where there was an opening which was not a window at the time. I'm going to mark this place here but from the other side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, you were not asked to mark anything. It was a question and you've answered the question. I think now Mr. Lukic will put the next question. Listen to the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So the next thing I asked you to do was to mark in this photograph, if possible, the approximate trajectory towards Nedzarici barracks?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. Let me try to orient myself. It is roughly this direction that would be the Nedzarici barracks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, to mark on a two-dimensional photograph a direction is pretty difficult - you'll understand that - because this photograph doesn't give any depth. So therefore it's not a very good instrument. If you have a better one, please use it. If not, be aware that it's not of great assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I do have a better one. I just kindly ask for this document to be saved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It will of saved and you want to tender it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections I take it, Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, the photograph marked by the witness will receive number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D345, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D345 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now have 1D12001 in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This photograph was supposed to -- or, rather, that photograph was supposed to have the same angle as this one from Google Earth. Can you find the Simon Bolivar school on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps with a bit of zooming in, I could find it. In the corner here it should be the airport on the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Three white lines, as far as I can see, that's where it's marked? In the middle, in the lower part? If you can. If you cannot --

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you zoom in a bit more, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have to go one -- I need something else. One up. One level up, if you want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One level of zooming, zoom out one level, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Up, up, in. Move to the right, please -- no, no, the other way. We have to zoom out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whatever, I'm not sure where the school is in this image. I cannot confirm that with any certainty, and that can only lead to further mistakes as we continue this discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. I asked if you could. If you cannot, no problem. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now we'll need another document. It's 1D1222.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This encircled building, is that the brigade command, the command of the Dobrinja Brigade?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is also a new photograph. This part above the marked building is the new shopping centre, Mercator, and I would kindly ask to see the details in the lower right-hand corner, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The photograph is the way it is. We cannot expand it any. If you can recognise it, you can. If you cannot, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since the buildings are all the same, the architecture is all the same, you cannot really recognise it. However, if this is the market, the shopping centre and the market together, then this would not be the command building. The command building was to the left. I assume this building that we can see on the very left, and we only see its beginning, if you will, the yellow facade, this and further up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Without being asked -- would you please refrain from marking if you're not asked to mark, but the witness marked the building which he thinks. He did it in blue and it's at the very left edge approximately one-third from the bottom in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This bit, not with a flat roof but with an entrance that is covered, what kind of facility is that?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, what was your question? What is what building?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This building, this edifice with windows on the roof.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the one that I marked?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think I understand. There is a construction in the very middle of this photograph with an entrance which is covered a few metres. I think Mr. Lukic would like you to tell us what that building is. It's the building with a white facade, with quite a number of windows in it and three, what seems to be, light openings or -- on the roof of that building.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] that could be that school. Given this east-west orientation, as far as I can see, the north is on the top of this page, and if we see the position of the gym on the far left, that could be that school. I'm not sure. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please place number 1 by the building that you think is the command building?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: However, with this level of zooming, I am not sure of that either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You marked in blue a building you said you thought, although you're not sure, to be the headquarters. Could you add a "1" to where you marked that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This other building with the windows on the roof and you say that maybe that is the Simon Bolivar school, could you place number 2 there.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this please be admitted into evidence and preserved as such?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D346, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When speaking of the incident that has to do with the Simon Bolivar school, is it correct that before the incident the water supply had stopped?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the incident? Throughout the war, Sarajevo was without water 90 per cent of the time, and my hands know that full well because from the water pump in Dobrinja I used to carry water home in jerrycans and all the inhabitants know that, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll focus you to the question. The question, and I'll slightly rephrase it, Mr. Lukic, whether prior to the incident, whether the water supply was interrupted. And if you know, tell us. If you don't know, or if you only have general knowledge about water situations, tell us that you don't have precise information.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The only imprecision is what does "prior" mean? Half an hour before the incident or seven days before the incident or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you give a time frame for when the water was -- supply had stopped?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The only thing that matters to me was that before that there was no water, and now the next question is supposed to clarify why. The population was explained -- was told that a water pump would be erected and that water would be distributed and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear the end of Mr. Lukic's statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Lukic, you were not fully understood until the very end. So your question really was whether there was no water supply at the time of the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before that, before that. At the time of the incident it was distribution of water actually in progress.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's totally unclear to me. You asked whether the water supply had stopped. Did you mean the water supply through the usual pipes, et cetera? Or would you mean other water supply? And if you asked whether it stopped, then you're asking for a change. That is, there is water, now there is no water anymore. If you don't give a time frame, it could have been 1989, it could have been whatever. So therefore, the witness, if he wishes to answer the question, asks what time frame before the incident? And then you said that's irrelevant. Therefore you were just asking whether there was a water supply immediately prior to the incident. Is that what you want to ask?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know whether there was immediately prior to the incident, whether there was water supply or whether there was no water supply?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I would like to know, Mr. Lukic, water supply to what? To the whole suburb or to the school?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was announced, as I understood it, that water distribution would be for the population of Dobrinja. But the witness can confirm or deny it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you heard the question? Is it correct that a day earlier, it had been announced that on the following day, water would be distributed in that place?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear that. At the time I lived in Dobrinja and I know that very rarely we had water coming out of faucets and there were water pumps where one had to pump water out of the soil by hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us look at 65 ter, Prosecution number, 10407. In e-court, we need the English version of this document, page 34. That's the page we need in English. No, I beg your pardon. In English, page 39, and in B/C/S, 34.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see here that Mrs. Azra Sisic on the 30th of June, 1995, gave a statement, and down there it says, "Statement:" "As for quite a while there has been no water in Sarajevo. Civilian protection officials organised the distribution of water in the Simon Bolivar school. On the 18th of June, 1995, at about 1000 hours I went to the mentioned school to get some drinking water." So you did not know that the civilian protection organised the distribution of water on the 18th of June?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour, is there dispute about distribution of water in the school on that very date and it being announced?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we just would stand by whatever is in the reports. There is no dispute that that's stated in the reports, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it's not contested as an untruthful statement given by this person?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, Mr. Lukic, you have your facts there provided by the Prosecution and the witness who was focusing on technical matters may not have known about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know that a water pump had been placed there on the day of the incident and that the pumping of water started around 11.00?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when the water pump was placed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Do you know that in this incident, the citizens of Dobrinja had been warned immediately before the incident that there was a danger of shelling?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Who would have issued such a warning?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The police?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have a look at 65 ter 10407, the Prosecution document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Not the same one on the screen already? That's what you asked for a few minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Give me a second, maybe. It is the same, I'm sorry. We need English version, page 41, and B/C/S version, page 37.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here, Mr. Muharem Mistric on the 1st of July, 1995, gave a statement where he said that as the civilian protection commissioner had received a written order, that every day he should install a pump at 6.00 in the morning by the Simon Bolivar school and to monitor the distribution of water: Due to the fact that the Dobrinja neighbourhood was often shelling, I did not want to install the pump but the residents brought their jerrycans and left them within the school compound. Then he goes on to say that he informed Mediha Citak, the MP commissioner, who issued a written order to him to start the pumping on distribution of water on the 18th of June, 1995. He also says that at around 10.00 on that day he arrived at the school with the intention of installing the pump. However, as there was a great crowd, he did not want to proceed with the distribution without the presence of police. And he consequently informed the MP commissioner so that at 11.00, three policemen arrived.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you are reading, I'm sorry, can you please tell me where is it? At the beginning of the statement, in the middle or where?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm reading from the beginning. And now, in 12th line, have you found it, towards the end? A 1. One of them told me that the pump was not safe and he ordered that the people waiting for water be removed into a safe premises. So that only two persons could have access to the pump, one to pump the water and the other one to prepare the jerrycans. Did you know that there were policemen present at the location and what their role was?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at all. This is the first time I see it. All I know is the technical aspects of the incidents, the azimuth and the rest of it. The way you are putting questions to me indicates that it was the fault of the residents who happened to be there where the bomb was going to be launched. How did they have the right to go there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're not supposed to comment on the questions put by Mr. Lukic. Just answer them. That's good enough. Mr. Lukic, were you seeking confirmation of those facts described in that statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm just asking the witness if he knows the facts. Now he says he does not know any facts prior to his investigation, and I will now move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so it's the knowledge of the witness you're interested in at this moment. Apparently he focused purely on his investigative task. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please help me, Mr. Lukic. You put the question: "Did you know that there were policemen presents at the location and what their role was?" And to that he answered: "No, no at all."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then later on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Only around the -- in relation to the question of the presence of the policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But then the witness said, "All I know is the technical aspects ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You asked only about the policemen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know that the civilian protection had organised the distribution of water?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By virtue of its function, the civilian protection was always involved in the distribution of humanitarian aid, and the water falls into that category.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please -- do not overlap.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness has told us that distribution of water, he considered that to be humanitarian aid. Do you have any specific knowledge about the distribution of water at that point in time, at that place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that time, and in that place, there was nothing special about distribution of water because there were several such places in Dobrinja, the civilian protection was there just to maintain order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The simple answer, then, is no. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your work, did you obtain information that in all incidents that happened in Dobrinja, the residents had been warned immediately prior to the incident that there was danger of shelling? And I will tell you which specific incidents I have in mind: In June of 1993, a football game; 12th of July, 1994, the queue for water at Spasenija Cana Babovic; 4th February 1994, distribution of humanitarian aid. Each and every time the police would come and warn the people, and an explosion took place immediately after that. Did you ever come across this information in your work?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time that I hear something like that, from you. I had never heard it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. You said that you are acquainted only with technical aspects, so let's speak about them. In relation to this incident, you established that the azimuth of the flights, in-flight of the shell was --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Lukic please repeat the degree.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 320 degrees, the angle.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which paragraph are you referring to? Which number?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the documents, can this be found, but if you can't remember right now, we can go through your documents as well. Can we therefore have Exhibit P2017, which is a Prosecution exhibit admitted yesterday? And we'll look at it in e-court. First you'll see what kind of document this is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Just since it looks like we are moving on from the last document can I ask that it be tendered into evidence since the witness has discussed it extensively?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean the exhibit with the statements of the witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Yes, 65 ter I believe it was 10407.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness said he has no knowledge. I don't know if I can tender that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, at the same time we discussed whether this was accepted by the Prosecution, the truthfulness of the statement, at least not in dispute that there were false statements. I think it is a document which might help us for other reasons as well, because it also gives further technical details about statements, but I also saw, for example, a -- seems to be useful information in the document. Any problem in --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would that be under a P number? I don't want to steal documents from them.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: We have no objection either way, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then, Mr. Registrar, could you assign a P number to the document we just looked at.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. 65 ter number 10407 will be Exhibit P2043.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document that you see in front of you and does it deal with the Simon Bolivar school?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, we still have the old document, at least on my screen. I still have the document that has just been admitted. Okay. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It seems to be P2017.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So do you recognise this document, Mr. Turkusic?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Among the individuals taking part in the investigation, there is your name as well; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is under number 5. And also there is a person from the KDZ under number 6, which was my organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at page 7 in this Prosecution document. I think it's page 7 in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you determine the azimuth that is plotted in the sketch?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the document on the right, where it says 320, and if it is north-south, it corresponds with the diagonal line that you see across the sketch, and that's the azimuth.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us now look at 1D1199.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You said 1D1119; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I misunderstood.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe I misspoke but we have the correct document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know why it's only in the B/C/S. Perhaps there is no translation. It should have been in the system. I'm going to read it quickly. This is a photo file. The shelling of the water pump, Simon Bolivar elementary school, 18th of June, 1995. Let's look at the next page. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not a document that I worked on or anyone else from my unit because of the heading, but it looks authentic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were asked whether you recognise it. Do I understand that you recognise the format? Have you seen it before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I am familiar with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So you recognise it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think so, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we need page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: By looking at these photographs, can you recognise whether this is consistent with the place of impact?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you please slowly read for us what the text is because we have no English translation. First, for the photograph on the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's under 3. It says -- should I read in B/C/S so I get correct English translation, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. No. Let me see. I'm perhaps lost. I'm looking at the original. One second. There is no English translation so what we would like you to do is to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Read B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- read B/C/S slowly so that we have at least some idea about what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Number 3: [Interpretation] "Number 3, the same, like the previous photograph, just photographed from a different direction. The arrow marks the place on the wall where the projectile impacted and exploded." [In English] If we can move up so I can see the next one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and the arrow apparently in this picture points at what seems to be the upper part of a wall, where there is some damage on the top. Yes. And what does the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Number 4. Number 2 and the arrow mark the place on the wall where the projectile impacted and exploded."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would need the end of page 2 in both versions and we'll have to move on to the third page. Then we need the next page. I do apologise. [In English] I need the previous document, P2017. My apologies. [Interpretation] Actually, no. The page is 2 and we need the third paragraph in the B/C/S, and also in the English version, we need this third paragraph on the same page where it says: "Precise measurements based on the characteristic traces caused by the blast of the shell on the concrete wall established that the shell had been fired from the north-westerly direction which corresponds to the aggressor's positions in the Nedzarici barracks." Now, on the basis of these precise measurements, a sketch was made, and we need -- now I just have the 65 ter number. That is this document that we've already admitted under a P number. 65 ter 10407 is the number. 65 ter. So we will get --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is now P2043.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In this document, we will need page 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you mark on this sketch the direction from which the shell arrived, and then could you mark north.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot at this moment because I find the details of the sketch to be unclear. I did not draw this, and I'm trying to decipher what means what. However, if, on the right-hand side, towards the bottom, this unusual arrow, a bit deformed, shows the point of impact on the wall, and the left-hand arrow on the left, with an S, shows the north, and this slight deviation could be it because it does differ from pure north. It is north-west. So I can only confirm that if S was "sjever," "north," then this is in correlation with this other arrow on the right that shows the deviation from the north which is an azimuth of a bit less than 360 but it is not pure west. So it is north/north-west. Is that what you're asking me to do because we have speculation here on the assumption that this S is north, "sjever," then that would be it. However, since I did not work on this sketch or image, it is something that relativises my answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you, you said north of north-west, which I would expect to be closer to north than to west. Is that what you intended to say? Because if we would draw an angle between -- if we could find an angle between the two arrows, wouldn't that be closer to north than to west?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you see 180 is south, 280 is pure west, and between 260 and 360 is the west. Now, whether that angle has what I explained just now, this could correspond to an azimuth of 320, or in more precise terms, it is better to give the azimuth actually in degrees rather than descriptively. It could correspond to a 320-degree azimuth. However, since I did not draw this sketch and I did not adjust the angles on the sketch to correspond to the situation on the ground, any comment of mine with regard to this image would be speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that pure west for you would be 270 degrees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. I think it's time for a break, Mr. Lukic. We would first like the witness to be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break and we resume at 20 minutes past mid-day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to show you a photograph. Actually it is a map. 1D1203. That's what we need.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Yes. Could I just get some information on who created this map and what it purports to be, and the date of the map, of course. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm not obviously swift enough. It was my intention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Harbour will patiently wait for your explanation, I'm certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On this map, we drew this line marked with number 1, and at the top of the map, we marked the north with the letter N. Would you agree that on this sketch -- or no, this map, this image, of Sarajevo, this line number 1 was placed in such a way that the wall that was hit by the shell corresponds or coincides with line number 1? Your answer was not recorded.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you then draw a line on this map that would, in your view, correspond to this direction and for it to be parallel with the wall that was hit by the shell?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. What should be parallel?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Parallel with the wall.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do you suggest that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No. The wall would be parallel to this line. The wall should be parallel to this line.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me -- do you want me to try to draw the wall on this map, its orientation as it is in nature?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear Mr. Lukic at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, what you apparently want to ask the witness is whether the line drawn on this map is parallel to the wall that was hit so that we know more or less the direction from one end to the wall to the other end of the wall, what that direction was. Can you confirm that, Witness, that it is parallel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I could if I were to do a bit of drawing on this map to help myself in terms of azimuth, east-west, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know what you want to draw on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: North is already on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: North is there already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did I understand correctly, Mr. Lukic, that this line north is drawn by you?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it possible to get north as indicated by the person who did the map rather than a line drawn by you?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Not in this size. It's at the end of the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
