utterances.text: But the simple question is, Mr. Lukic, whether the witness can confirm that the -- from the beginning until the end of a straight wall, whether, if you would put a compass there, that it would indicate that it was going from 207, the lower part, 207 degrees or was it 217? I don't have it. 207 to 207 minus 180? Because that's the direction. Two points define the direction. And on the compass you say this is on the compass a line between 207 and 27 degrees? That's the simple question, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know if this 207, what does that mean? I'm just interested in this line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Who put the 207 in it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know who put the 207.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The 207 -- so you drew the line?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I didn't draw it. Must be some meaning but unknown to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The most likely meaning would be, if you look at north, west, south, east, I would not be surprised if the direction downwards at the compass would be 207 degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I understand it, yes. Probably it's where the number 1 is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the witness has not drawn it. We don't need an expert or a witness for that, we just need a compass for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If he can orientate himself and see if it's this line, red line, through the middle of this picture is parallel to the wall, as you said from one side to another side, hit by the grenade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The direction of the wall, would that be parallel, or even exactly the same, as the line drawn under number 1? That was the question. Can you answer it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] However, with the proviso that we are looking at a map whose provenance I don't know and Mr. Lukic doesn't know either so we are basing all of this on speculation, on the assumption that N is really north. Then the line is roughly here, the one that I drew, west. Now, the -- the shell would arrive -- well, let me mark it with a D. Roughly. And then in that case, this line marked number 1 could be a line in space that is this azimuth 207 given all these assumptions, if, if, if, maybe it's this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're not answering the question unfortunately. First of all, you're marking without being invited to do so. Would you please refrain from doing that. Second, Mr. Lukic, I did not understand that where the 207 is written, that that is the position where a shell impacted or is it, in your question? I thought it was somewhere in Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I thought it's down there where it says Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So therefore, the marking is totally misplaced, Witness. Could it be erased?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honours if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I think it's clear from Your Honour's questioning and from the witness's response and the witness's subsequent marking that the markings on this map are confusing. There is no foundation for them. Even Mr. Lukic doesn't know where they originated. I'm wondering if there isn't a better map perhaps one in the investigative file that can be used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not about the maps. I mean, it is about the wall. I mean, if you know where the wall is and how it is -- what its place is in the building, then it's easy to project that on a map. There is nothing wrong with the map apart from whether it's a nowadays map or whether it's a map from --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry for interrupting, Your Honour. One clarification. My colleague Stojanovic just informed me that this map is received from the OTP. It's from their collection. Only we used it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you added --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Probably it's enlarged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you did put a line, 1, on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The map simply is a map of Sarajevo. Let's not make any fuss about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it is oriented that north is on the top.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I've seen many maps of Sarajevo and whether it's exactly or not is a different matter but at least the upper part is what I've seen many, many times as being depicted as the north. So let's forget about the map. The problem is the wall. We need precise information about the school and about the wall in order to be able to project that on a map. Therefore, if in any of the reports we find a precise location of the wall, then we could see whether, if projected on a map where north is known, whether that would result in the line Mr. Lukic has drawn. That is the exercise I think we have to do if we want to move forward. Mr. Lukic, anywhere in the report, anything known about how exactly the wall was situated? Because that's what we need, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's why we started with that picture first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then we moved also to wider area from Google Earth, but the witness wasn't able to orientate himself on that Google Earth map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then we are trying now with the Sarajevo map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but the problem is that the wall is not visible on this map, and that is what we need. And if I would want to establish that, I would choose Google Earth. I would zoom in until the very, very detail of the building. Then we would have to establish whether the building, which existed at that time, is similar to the building at this moment, as far as directions are concerned. Then we would have to find exactly the wall we are talking about. And we would then need to know whether that is sufficiently defined to establish what the direction of the line of that wall is. That's what is needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we try, then, that exercise with 1D1201?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm happy whatever way you want to access it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: If Mr. Lukic is open to this suggestion? In the investigative file which is now in evidence, although I don't recall the P number, it's 65 ter 10407, on page 2 of the B/C/S version there is a map and there are clear structures indicated whereby the witness may be able to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's a drawing or a map?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: It's a map. There is a drawing on top of it but the witness may be able to indicate or confirm as you've asked him to do with the other one if that is the direction the wall was facing. And Ms. Stewart has informed me that this is Exhibit P2043.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't have those numbers. Which number was it before, 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can I use the time to put one question to the witness. Do you recognise on this map in front of you where the school we are talking about is situated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that at any rate this is not the place where we have this deflection of the red line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This was not my question. Do you know where the school we are talking about is situated on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm trying. I believe it's in the area a little beneath the middle of the map where you see the word "Dobrinja," so where Dobrinja is written, so somewhere in that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we zoom in on that part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And then my next question: Have you any idea how that school with the wall we are talking about, the wall where the -- of impact, would be situated in relation to the red line? If not, let me know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that the orientation of this red line could be parallel with the wall that was hit. Or, rather, that they are positioned along the same line or direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Perhaps that helps you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me also ask a question before -- it's going to be directed unfortunately to you, Mr. Lukic, because you know more about this red line. What does this red line represent?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Simply to show us, because we'll have to deal with this direction, the direction of the wall in the space on the map. It's not possible to deal with it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't understand what you say when you say "direction of the wall in space."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Position --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I try to assist? If you have a wall, a wall has a certain length.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you extend those dots.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And has hardly any volume apart from that. If you extend the line from the beginning to the end of the wall known, that is what you wanted to depict on this photograph, I take it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And I don't understand. Then I'm lost. If this is what is depicting the length of the wall, I would imagine the wall to be inside here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If this is a wall, looking on a wall, the only thing you did is to take the beginning and the end of the wall and draw a long line so as to know how that wall is facing what direction because that seems to be what your exercise is about. So that we know the position of the wall on 360-degrees compass map. Is that what you intended to do?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's just easier for us to see on the map because wall is too small for us to follow. This way we have the line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In my view, the problem is resolved with the last answer of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think I can continue. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can. Perhaps I have one. Witness, you have -- you lived in Dobrinja, I think you told us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we further zoom in on this map, a little bit further even, you see S diacritic K, and a red rectangle, a very small one, next to what seems to be an envelope. Do you have any recollection --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any recollection on whether a school would be situated there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is possible, if you look at the street below, the yellow one, and the one above the school which is rather a pedestrian path, I think that it's realistic to assume that this is the position of the school in Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We needed this line for the next map. We are going to make a proposition for you, a proper one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 1D1204. [In English] Nothing is drawn on this one, but only I would offer the first one, 1203, into evidence, 1D1203.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honours it still hasn't -- there still hasn't been a foundation established for all the markings on the map. And what's most concerning to me is this number 207. We don't know where it came from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But give me one second during the next break and I'll be able on the basis of this map, if printed out for me, to confirm whether it's the line is 207, yes or no, on a 360-degree scale. So therefore, if it's anything else, I'll let you know. The concern is not a serious one at this moment. And --

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I guess the additional point is that while it may be possible to confirm this over the break with your compass, we don't know what the relevance is of that number. Mr. Lukic hasn't indicated how that's important or what his case is involving that number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic has asked the witness whether the -- let's use again the word "direction of the wall" but the orientation of the wall was in accordance with the red line. The witness confirmed that. And therefore, it's -- if it's 207, then the wall is 207, at least that is what the witness tells us at this moment. Whether reliable or not is still to be further to be seen, but that's the relevance. There is no doubt about that, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, if it's clear to you what the relevance is of the angle of the wall, it's not clear to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The relevance of the angle of the wall will play a role in further, I take it, exploring the damage on the wall and the possible impact on the wall so as to establish what may be the origin of fire. That's the relevance.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I defer to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and of course in re-examination you can challenge all of it, that it's 207, that it's the orientation of the wall, whatever, but let's first allow Mr. Lukic to further develop his line of questioning. And you wanted it to be admitted to Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Objections are overruled.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. 65 ter number 1D1203 will be Exhibit D347.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D347 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have one strange question for the Registrar. 347 has one or two pages?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it's a one-page map.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have wanted to show another map, but I cannot locate it right now. I will proceed with this statement, and it seems that it is redacted. I don't know if we should go to private session or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know what it is, I don't know why it is redacted, so therefore I have to rely on you, Mr. Lukic. Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I would suggest that we go into private session to discuss this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know that UNPROFOR also came to the scene of this incident at the time?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you aware of their conclusions?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On some occasion during some previous testimony and leafing through certain documents, I don't know exactly when, yes, I heard about the conclusion regarding the direction, and I absolutely cannot accept that because of imprecision.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that, actually, you marked the direction of the north, one that significantly differs from the sketches on the scene?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't find your question clear at all. What kind of sketches are you talking about? Show them to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your work, did you mark the north?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. Everything that I did and that my colleagues did in the unit that I was in, this orientation, south-north, generally speaking we would always mark that, but when we would write the azimuth, then one would know that is the most precise way of marking orientation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that in actual fact you determined the direction at 270 degrees but that you marked it as 320?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, could I have the original document? Fifteen or 20 years have elapsed, whatever. I cannot keep all these figures in my head. Could I please have my report? Could it please be displayed on the screen, in order to refresh my memory?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would need a break to locate that exactly in your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But now briefly, 1D1199, could we take a look at that briefly. In this document, we need page 5. One page ahead, please, page 6. Obviously, something went awry with e-court. Could we see page 4? [In English] I'm sorry, but I will have to ask for early break. Something -- sorry, I will have to ask for early break. Something went wrong with my numbers and e-court so I have to sort it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Lukic, you'll get an early break. But first could we ask the witness to be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take that break. I have, however, one question. It's in cross-examination, it turned out that there are more reports or sketches or photographs of the incident. Would it be possible to have a full account of every contemporaneous report that was written specifically on this incident so that we are not missing any of it, that we know what material does exist?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I believe that the file that was introduced, which was 65 ter 10407, includes all of the sketches and reports but does not include the photographs. But I will double check that and I will make sure that if it doesn't, that I assemble a document that does and we can, if Mr. Lukic agrees, just submit that entire file rather than what's currently in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, you read from a document which was not in English, and you read the subtitles to photographs. You read the titles of photograph 3 and photograph 4, if you remember. Now, photograph 3, I think, starts with referring to photograph 2. When looking at that material, I had great difficulties in finding on photograph 2 exactly what was depicted in more detail in photograph 3. Photograph 3 and 4 have arrows, light blue arrows, which point at what should need our attention. I didn't find similar arrows on 2 but I may have missed them because they are very flawed. Could the parties in one way or another reach an agreement on what of photograph 2 is detailed in photographs 3 and 4 and then inform the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I would be happy to meet with Mr. Lukic about this, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Not during this break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no. Because you have other difficulties. We are not done with this witness today anyhow. You have the whole afternoon and sunny evening to further study photographs 2, 3 and 4. We take a break and resume at 1.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness will be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. Lukic, I hope that you have resolved some of your problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, with the help of our Case Manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You asked me to show you the sketch that you drew. I said you but in actual fact I meant the service. So you're going to tell me if you didn't draw it personally.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P2017 is what we need. We need page 7 in this document. Actually, do I apologise. Perhaps we should move page by page because this consists of several documents actually. So let us start with the first page and let us leaf through the pages one by one so that the witness could see and could tell us which document is his. So page 2 now, please. Page 3. Page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think it would be better if you asked if he has prepared this document because we are now moving to the next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This first document, before the one we see now, did you prepare that or somebody else?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first one that you showed me, as you were leafing through the pages one by one, it said centre of security services, CSB, where I was an associate member of the team but others compiled this document. However, I did work on its elaboration.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that this also answers the Judge's question. Now let us move on to the next page. This document is from your service; right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We can see from the top of the page that it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Can we move on to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My signature is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Next page now. [In English] Can we go to the next page? [Interpretation] Now we see a document that says the shelling of Sarajevo. Now it, I don't know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you go to that document, I didn't see the end of the document in the English version of the previous document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I saw the one in B/C/S where the signature is but I didn't see -- that's better.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's the last page, actually second page of that KDZ in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you're so precise, it's the third page. The last one is the third page in English. There are two pages in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In B/C/S, sorry, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we move on now to the next page. [Microphone not activated] Sorry, I didn't turn on my microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document, was it compiled by the CSB or your service, KDZ?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I cannot see on the top of the page who compiled it, it's probably contained in the signature, but I think it was the KDZ in terms of the format because the azimuth was 320, like in the previous document that you showed us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We need the next page now, please. On this sketch -- actually, what does this represent? How many degrees, this straight line?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I assume that there is a northerly orientation, that would be the azimuth, 320 degrees. So there are 60 missing to 380 so that would precisely be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was listening to the English interpretation. I don't know if you said this, 320, so we need 60 to 380.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Exact north.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You probably misspoke.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I probably did. I'm a bit tired. So it's 40 degree to reach the exact north. Thank you. Thank you for correcting me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind this wall which is damaged and the calculation of the degree of the shell impact, would you agree that the direction established should be between 270 and 300 degrees, roughly speaking?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, because it suggests this ambiguity and uncertainty, when you quoted someone from UNPROFOR who described this direction in very ambiguous terms, by just relying on the cardinal points, and this is something that a lay person would do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 1D1231. I have to admit that we uploaded this during the break, which is actually a continuation of the previous map, but due to my error, I failed to give it to our Case Manager to upload it into the system in time. However, frankly speaking, I don't understand what is depicted here by our experts, and therefore I cannot put any questions relating to this photograph and I'm not going to seek this document to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since we most likely will not conclude today, you might seek further advice.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I might.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will try to do that. I just wanted to inform the Prosecution that now it's in the system, and Mr. Turkusic to try to see what it depicts, and we will continue based on this photo tomorrow, if I understand even in the afternoon what it is about. But at least I was -- before the break when I asked -- before the break asked for the correct page only, I was shown only the top part, and the picture I was asking for was in the bottom part of the picture so I need again 1D1199. And I need page 5, lower part.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is part of the photo file relating to the Simon Bolivar school, and you did the same in other cases where you cited a series of shells, actually, their serial numbers and to which batch they belonged.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that a question?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can this photograph show -- did you pay attention and was it possible to see the serial number when you were photographing the stabiliser?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that my colleagues from the KDZ shot a series of photographs and I believe that among those photographs there is one showing the serial number, and such photograph must be recorded in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I tried on the screen at least to enlarge it and I failed to find it but it wasn't you who took this photograph. I'm not going to ask you anything further.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously the purpose of this photograph was not to detect the serial number but, rather, to depict the tail-fin of the shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. As we told you, we are going to go back to the map of Sarajevo with some markings. Can we now move to paragraphs 28 and 29 of your statement? It deals with the shelling of Titova Street of 9 April 1995. You said in paragraph 28 that you didn't remember that incident but it was a typical one for the reports that I prepared on the consequences of shelling. My question is: Is it possible that you did not take part in this investigation but that someone put your name or maybe even signed your name?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That never happened, because we had such a plethora of trace evidence so that we relied only on those that we can be sure of. If you have initials and somebody else signing it, that happened only that someone prepares a report but is absent the following day, then a colleague would sign on his behalf, but that was all done with the knowledge of the chief of the department, and by signing this on somebody's behalf, it's been authenticated. Otherwise, it never happened that somebody else would prepare a report and have it signed by somebody who is not familiar with the details contained in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Next paragraphs 30 and 31, we are going to speed up the process. It's the shelling of Safeta Zajke, shelling of 24th May 1995. That was a time when the BH Army was attempting to break the circle around Sarajevo by launching an offensive. This is what the evidence we have in this case shows.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with that. We have been trying the whole time to break the circle around the city, probably the strongest one in the history, and that is what we did on this occasion as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we need 1D1225 in e-court. Can we zoom in. That's good.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you mark the position of the location on Safeta Zajke Street number 43?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot find Safeta Zajke Street, but this is the location, Alipasin Most in Novi Grad municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have it marked at the end of the street called Esada Midzica Street. Would that be consistent?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Help me a bit more and tell me where is it in the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's this industrial area above the railway tracks called Boljakov Potok. And under that you have Tvornica Zice, which is a wire factory.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's that part of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So can you put number 1 at the bottom of Esada Midzica Street, if it is consistent more or less with the position of Safeta Zajke number 43.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I'm going to mark something, I need to be really sure about that, and from memory, I cannot confirm that this is Safeta Zajke Street. I haven't checked any maps recently, so I can do it only on the basis of your suggestion. All I can say is that this is the relevant area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. We can see the RMK wire factory in the vicinity, and to the left of the factory we can see Energoinvest. This is a reinforced iron factory, in fact, Energoinvest?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Iron cast factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that during the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina, these two locations were used to manufacture weapons?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible, but I don't have such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us just briefly look at 1D1207. [In English] I'm sorry, can we admit unmarked part of this city, since the gentleman was talking about the area and we discussed some factories in this map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, Mr. Lukic, can I just confirm, did you say Esada Midzica is the same now as Safeta Zajke?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What I have, I have circle at the end of Esada Midzica and it joins with this horizontal road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what is that horizontal road because the heading here is "shelling of Safeta Zajke Street"? And we haven't seen it. The witness said he couldn't see that street here and I haven't seen it myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just need a map because he confirmed that that's the area. I'm not familiar with that part of the city, trust me, and probably we will have to clarify it in the future but now I don't know whether it's the new or old name for the street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Seems to be typical, something to be agreed upon by the parties. You look at the old map, you look at the new map, and then agree on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Another subject for the short meeting with Mr. Lukic, Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: That's an acceptable avenue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we MFI this, then, map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Seems to be no problem, Ms. Harbour, is there?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: No, no problem with MFI'ing. And when we have our discussion perhaps you could also provide the date or any other relevant information about the map. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The map will be -- yes, the Chamber is inclined to admit it into evidence. We have a lot of maps without any further markings, and then we have a basis for your later agreement that the parties agree that what on this map in evidence is called street so and so bears the name now -- no, what -- what used to have that name, I do not know whether it's an old map or a new map, and then to agree on that and then the map is the basis in evidence for any further agreement. Until now it's just a map. Yes. Then Mr. Registrar, this --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. 65 ter number 1D1225 will be Exhibit D348.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. After confirmation of the numbers, D348 is admitted into evidence and the parties are invited to use this as a basis for any agreement on the location of the shelling incident. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. First I'd like to show 1D1206. In this document, we need the second page, the penultimate paragraph, which says, "Military industry." Among other things, we see the wire factory mentioned here, that unknown types and make of shells and grenades are being charged on the premises.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do we not have an English translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Not yet. We do not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Then you could please be a bit more precise where we can see what you have just said and perhaps read that line into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Subtitle I will start from there, and I'll read: [Interpretation] "Military industry," first bullet point: "'Piva,' shell charges for mortar 82 and 60 millimetres." Second bullet point: "'Vaso Miskin Crni.' Production of mine bodies for mortars of 82 and 60 millimetres. Different types of hand grenades and for rifle grenades and infantry ammunition." And the third bullet point, the one that I pointed out to the witness: "'Astra,' 'factory,' 'ZICE,' and the tobacco factory, charges for different types of mines and shells and grenades."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you tell us where the document comes from? To be short, what is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says here that this is an intelligence document of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What's the witness expected to do with this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Too many microphones must be open. I'll switch mine off again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. What is the witness supposed to do with this?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, now I cannot turn on mine. Sorry. Thank you. He's supposed to confirm whether it is the same factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How many wire factories were there in Sarajevo, Tvornica Zice, is that the same one that we saw on the map the other time when we were talking about that? Could you confirm that, Mr. Turkusic, that what is meant here is precisely the wire factory that we saw earlier on?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you use this expression, Tvornica Zice, the wire factory, there was only one in Sarajevo. However, at the end of the document it says that the information is suspicious and that it needs to be checked. At the very end of this page that I see --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As far as I can read this document, this pertains to the heading above that that speaks about military prisons. That they are in the former JNA barracks, Viktor Bubanj, and the central prison for Serbs, the silo in Tarcin?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document starts by defining certain Muslim forces in Sarajevo that I had never heard of and I spent the entire war in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You want it to be marked for identification, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because there is no translation so therefore we cannot possibly admit it at this moment. No objection against it being marked. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. 65 ter number 1D1206 will be MFI D349.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And keeps that status for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I'd like to ask for 1D1207 in e-court, please. I'd like to move into private session, briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Should be "122 millimetres." It's in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But on the transcript it says "22."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. It's the end of our day. I'm afraid that we will have to continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we are about to adjourn for the day, Mr. Turkusic, and we would like to see you back tomorrow morning. And I again instruct you that you should not speak or communicate in whatever way with whomever about your testimony. We would like to see you back at 9.30 in the morning in this same courtroom, III. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I hardly dare to ask. Are you on track as far as time is concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I hardly dare to respond. I'm not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you at least try to be as organised as possible, and to focus directly and not deal with matters which are easily agreed upon, I take it, and that is not only names of streets but what is in a report or -- apart from whether it's true or not but there is a lot of things I think that can be dealt with in a more efficient way and you are invited to consider that overnight. We adjourn for the day and we will resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 29th of August at 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 29th day of August, 2013, at 9.30 a.m. 24 25
